newsitem.title: USA: NYS says bond firms' donations won't sway awards.
newsitem.headline: NYS says bond firms' donations won't sway awards.

text.p: The Administration of New York State Gov. George Pataki on Wednesday promised that its selections of underwriting firms would not be swayed by big donations a state senator said the firms made to campaign committees.
A spokesman for Gov Pataki said, "It would have no effect on the administration's underwriting decisions."

New York State Senator Franz Leichter, D-Manhattan, released a report that showed that state Republicans got almost $1 million in campaign contributions in 1995 and 1996 from municipal bond underwriting firms that were awarded profitable underwriting contracts.

While Pataki, a Republican, did not get direct contributions from the firms, the state senator said the Republican governor was aided by the almost $1 million in donations that underwriters gave Republican comittees.

Those committees were the National Republican Senatorial Committee, two bodies set up to campaign for the approval of the 1996 Clean Water/Clean Air Bond Act, and the Republican State Committee's "housekeeping" account.
Voters last November approved the $1.75 billion envirnomental bond act and the Pataki Administration and the legislature are working out how much of these funds will be spent this year.
